provenance: M7 phase 1 (docs/evals/evaluation-methodology.md, 'Verifier accuracy estimation'). Replays evals/labels/verifier-sample.jsonl — 25 hand-labeled runs captured by evals/labels/capture.py, all of which reached the runtime verify() call agent.py:491 makes with NO expect and NO state — through the exact same call, offline, against the committed JSONL. PRE-FIX (phase 1, verifier.py unchanged, 24 records — chunked-dump-cheapest below did not exist yet): tp=10, fp=12, fn=1, tn=1 — precision = 10/22 = 0.4545, recall = 10/11 = 0.9091. The 12 FPs were trap-near-miss-entity, trap-wrong-field, trap-unsorted-cheapest, trap-search-not-executed, trap-form-not-submitted, trap-wrong-cell-total, probe5-shop-listing-dump, live-wrong-field-upc, live-wrong-field-submitter, live-unsorted-cheapest, live-wrong-field-availability, probe5-books-travel-dump; the 1 FN was unverified-click-correct-answer (click carried no expected_state so actions_verified tripped even though the extracted answer was right); the 1 TN was unverified-click-wrong-answer, failed the same way. POST-FIX (M7 phase 2: verifier.py gained the `not_a_dump` L1 check, DUMP_RATIO=0.35 over len(clean(value))/len(clean(page_text))): 24 records gave tp=10, fp=10, fn=1, tn=3 — precision = 10/20 = 0.50, recall = 10/11 = 0.9091 (unchanged; the check never touches a correct answer). Exactly the two predicted flips happened, FP -> TN: probe5-shop-listing-dump (ratio 0.52) and probe5-books-travel-dump (ratio 0.45), both well clear of the 0.35 threshold and the 0.18 ceiling measured on every non-dump extraction in the whole fast suite. POST-CHUNKING-RECORD (M7 final phase, cold review): `not_a_dump` closes only the single-extraction dump shape — verify() never receives the task text, so N per-row extractions are structurally identical whether the task asked for all rows or for one. Demonstrated with the 25th record, `chunked-dump-cheapest`: same task and fixture as probe5-shop-listing-dump ('which product is the cheapest, and what is its price?', shop.html) but the plan chunks the sorted catalogue into four separate `{role: listitem, index: 0..3}` extractions instead of one whole-container extraction; the answer is still all four products, but each extraction's own ratio is ~12% of its evidence window, far under 0.35, so `not_a_dump` passes all four and the runtime verifier returns PASS on a page dump. Matrix moves to tp=10, fp=11, fn=1, tn=3 — precision = 10/21 = 0.4762, recall = 10/11 = 0.9091 (unchanged; the new record is labeled `wrong`, predicted PASS, so it is a new FP, not a TP/FN/TN). The other 10 pre-existing FPs are untouched by design — they are focused, mechanically-clean, WRONG answers (wrong field, wrong row, unsorted list, unexecuted search/submit) that this check was never meant to catch; L1's blind spot for semantic responsiveness (see verifier.py's module docstring) is real and still open, and the chunking evasion is the same blind spot in a different shape. This remains a floor reading of a small, deliberately adversarial sample, not a general accuracy claim; see evals/labels/verifier-sample.jsonl for every record and its hand-written label.

triage.note: pins a measurement, not a guarantee. Moving this expect is a decision like a baseline move (CLAUDE.md hard rule 1): both moves above followed a recorded change — the M7 phase 2 move followed a `verifier.py` change (the not_a_dump L1 check), the final-phase move followed a recorded new label (chunked-dump-cheapest), never a quiet edit to make this case pass.
triage.does_not_grade: the remaining fp=10 pre-existing false positives are the honest residue: a short, plausible, WRONG answer still passes L1 whenever it is focused rather than a dump. The 11th FP (chunked-dump-cheapest) is a different residue: a page dump split across several focused-looking extractions, which not_a_dump was designed to catch and does not, because it is evaluated per-extraction with no task text. Only ground-truth L2 (a live run has none) or an evidence-only LLM check (L3, absent by design) closes either gap.
